title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 1:1
body: “Paul, called to be an Apostle of Jesus Christ, through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, unto the Church of God which is at Corinth, even them that are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be Saints, with all that call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, their Lord and ours: Grace unto you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 1

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 1:4
body: “I thank my God always concerning you, for the Grace of God which was given you in Jesus Christ; that in every thing you were enriched in him.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 2

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 1:18
body: “For the word of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but to us which are saved it is the power of God. For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the prudence of the prudent will I reject.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 4

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 2:1
body: “And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God. For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 6

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 2:6
body: “Howbeit we speak wisdom among the perfect, yet a wisdom not of this world, nor of the rulers of this world, which are coming to naught; but we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, even the wisdom that hath been hidden, which God fore-ordained before the worlds unto our glory.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 7

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 3:1
body: “And I, brethren, could not speak unto you as unto spiritual, but as unto Carnal, as unto babes in Christ. I fed you with milk, and not with meat: for ye were not yet able to bear it; nay, not even now are ye able.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 8

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 3:12
body: “If any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, stubble; each man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire shall prove each man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he built thereon, he shall receive a reward.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 9

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 3:18
body: “Let no man deceive himself. If any man (enhumin omitted.) thinketh that he is wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may become wise.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 10

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 4:3
body: “But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man's judgment: yea I judge not mine own self. For I know nothing against myself, yet am I not hereby justified: but He that judgeth me is the Lord.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 11

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 4:10
body: “Whereas the others prided themselves on the things which are contrary to these, on wisdom, glory, wealth, consideration.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 13

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 4:17
body: “For this cause have I sent unto you Timothy, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who shall put you in remembrance of my ways which be in Christ Jesus.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 14

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 5:1
body: “It is actually reported that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not even named among the Gentiles, that one of you hath his father's wife. And ye are puffed up, and did not rather mourn, that he that had done this deed might be taken away from among you.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 15

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 5:9
body: “I wrote unto you in my epistle to have no company with fornicators: yet not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or with the covetous and extortioners, or with idolaters, for then must ye needs go out of the world: but now I write unto you not to keep company, if any man that is named a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a drunkard, or a reviler, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 16

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 6:12
body: “Here he glances at the gluttons. For since he intends to assail the fornicator again, and fornication arises from luxuriousness and want of moderation, he strongly chastises this passion.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 17

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 6:15
body: “Having passed on from the fornicator to the covetous person, he comes back to the former from the latter, no longer henceforth discoursing with him but with the others who had not committed fornication. And in the act of securing them lest they fall into the same sins, he assails him again.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 18

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 7:1
body: “Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote to me: it is good for a man not to touch a woman. But because of fornications, let each man have his own wife; and let each woman have her own husband.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 19

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 8:1
body: “Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffeth up, but love edifieth.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 20

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 11:2
body: “Now I praise you that ye remember me in all things, and hold fast the traditions, even as I delivered them to you.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 26

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 12:1
body: “Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. Ye know that when ye were Gentiles, ye were led away unto those dumb idols, howsoever ye might be led.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 29

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Corinthians 15:1
body: “Now I make known unto you, brethren, the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye received, wherein also ye stand; by which also ye are saved: in what words I preached it unto you.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 38
